projects.name: NimbusFlow Field Service App
projects.description: Offline-first .NET and Blazor field-service application for maintenance teams.
projects.objective: Prove that Cognitive Memory can separate app architecture, offline sync, auditability, privacy, and rollout concerns from detailed project-structure source data.

nodes.title: Product workflows
nodes.subtitle: Dispatcher, technician, and manager loops
nodes.notes: Dispatchers plan routes and assign work packages. Technicians capture inspections, parts, photos, and signatures while offline. Operations managers review audit history, SLA performance, repeat failures, and safety exceptions.

nodes.title: Architecture boundaries
nodes.subtitle: UI, application services, domain, infrastructure
nodes.notes: Blazor components orchestrate rendering and user intent. Application services own workflow rules. Domain objects own work-order, inspection, asset, inventory, and scheduling invariants. Infrastructure owns PostgreSQL, object storage, ERP imports, notifications, and local-device sync channels.

nodes.title: Offline sync and conflict review
nodes.subtitle: Idempotent command batches
nodes.notes: Mobile clients submit command batches with device id, idempotency key, device timestamp, server-received timestamp, source form schema version, and attachment hashes. Non-overlapping form edits can merge automatically; asset status, part consumption, and safety sign-off conflicts require human review.

nodes.title: Source evidence and auditability
nodes.subtitle: Attachments remain evidence
nodes.notes: Photos, signatures, sensor readings, and uploaded documents are source evidence. Generated summaries may reference them but cannot replace them. Audit exports must include source locators, hashes, actor ids, timestamps, redaction status, and decision history.

nodes.title: Customer privacy risk
nodes.subtitle: Photos may include private content
nodes.notes: Field photos can accidentally include customer private data, badges, whiteboards, or home interiors. Upload processing needs redaction state, retention rules, thumbnail restrictions, and role-based access before pilot.

nodes.title: Offline regression test plan
nodes.subtitle: Conflict, replay, and attachment coverage
nodes.notes: Test with network interruption, duplicate command batches, schema-version mismatch, clock skew, conflicting asset status, part inventory lag, corrupted attachment upload, and explicit conflict resolution.

nodes.title: Pilot rollout
nodes.subtitle: Two teams and one warehouse
nodes.notes: Pilot with two maintenance crews, one dispatcher group, and one warehouse. Success requires offline capture reliability, dispatcher override confidence, conflict-review SLA, and audit export accepted by operations.

projects.name: LedgerLift SaaS Business Plan
projects.description: Commercial plan for month-end close coordination SaaS for small accounting firms.
projects.objective: Give Cognitive Memory a non-code business-plan project with market, packaging, compliance, pricing, and go-to-market assumptions.

nodes.title: Target market segment
nodes.subtitle: Small accounting firms
nodes.notes: Primary buyers are partners and operations leads in five-to-fifty-person accounting firms. Daily users are staff accountants and client controllers coordinating recurring evidence collection across many monthly close clients.

nodes.title: Workflow wedge
nodes.subtitle: Month-end close accountability
nodes.notes: Initial wedge is recurring close checklists, role assignments, document requests, exception tracking, and client-visible status summaries. The product displaces spreadsheets by reducing lost requests and ambiguous ownership.

nodes.title: Pricing and packages
nodes.subtitle: Starter, Growth, Firm
nodes.notes: Starter covers ten clients, checklist templates, document requests, and status dashboard. Growth covers fifty clients, reusable exceptions, role assignments, client portal, and audit export. Firm covers unlimited clients, advanced permissions, API access, SSO, and retention policy.

nodes.title: Compliance timing
nodes.subtitle: SOC 2 and retention questions
nodes.notes: Open question: whether SOC 2 Type I is required before first paid pilots. Evidence retention must distinguish client documents, workflow metadata, generated summaries, and audit exports. AI summarization could be a differentiator or a compliance concern.

nodes.title: Go-to-market motion
nodes.subtitle: Partner-led pilots
nodes.notes: Start with founder-led discovery and paid pilots. Use close-cycle retrospectives to quantify time saved, missing-document reduction, client-response latency, and staff accountability. Avoid broad enterprise messaging until retention and SSO are proven.

nodes.title: Success metrics
nodes.subtitle: Cycle time, exceptions, adoption
nodes.notes: Track monthly active firms, client account activation, checklist completion latency, unresolved exceptions at close cutoff, evidence request aging, audit export usage, churn risk by client count, and support tickets per firm.

nodes.title: AI summary risk
nodes.subtitle: Generated summaries are not source truth
nodes.notes: AI summaries must cite evidence and keep source documents authoritative. The business plan must not promise autonomous accounting judgment. Summary features should start as review aids with clear source links and export controls.

projects.name: Docker Delivery Platform Analysis
projects.description: Analysis of local Docker Compose, CI image builds, staging deployment, and production promotion.
projects.objective: Provide source data for memory about Docker delivery practices, PostgreSQL test databases, worker isolation, and provider-specific service boundaries.

nodes.title: Image promotion
nodes.subtitle: Build once, promote by digest
nodes.notes: Images are built once per commit and promoted by digest. Promotion metadata includes commit, build number, source branch, base image digest, vulnerability scan result, and migration compatibility state.

nodes.title: Local Compose profiles
nodes.subtitle: Required and optional services
nodes.notes: Compose is the local-development contract. Required profile includes app and PostgreSQL. Optional profiles add Redis, Qdrant, MinIO, mail capture, and worker containers. Optional services must not be required for relational-only smoke tests.

nodes.title: Branch-named PostgreSQL smoke DB
nodes.subtitle: Fresh DB per behavior test
nodes.notes: Cognitive-memory behavior smoke uses a new PostgreSQL database per task. SQLite is allowed only for compatibility or EF model tests. The app should expose active provider status before running memory behavior checks.

nodes.title: Secrets policy
nodes.subtitle: No secrets in Compose or image layers
nodes.notes: Local developer secrets are injected from user profiles or secure stores. CI secrets use short-lived credentials. Compose files reference variables but do not contain secret values.

nodes.title: Readiness checks
nodes.subtitle: App, migration, dependency state
nodes.notes: Health checks must distinguish process alive, HTTP ready, database reachable, migrations applied, external provider configured, worker queues accepting jobs, and optional projection providers unavailable by design.

nodes.title: Worker boundaries
nodes.subtitle: Hosted background service or separate container
nodes.notes: Projection and consolidation workers should use deterministic job packets, leases, input hashes, algorithm versions, schema identifiers, and acceptance validation. Workers cannot mutate authoritative memory directly.

nodes.title: Docker risks
nodes.subtitle: Volumes, cache, service drag
nodes.notes: Compose volumes can preserve stale schemas across branches. Image layer cache can hide package restore failures. Running all optional services locally slows feedback. Use explicit provider-unavailable errors rather than silent fallbacks.

projects.name: Regional Inflation And Labor Market Brief
projects.description: Economic brief about inflation, wage growth, housing costs, and small-business hiring constraints.
projects.objective: Give Cognitive Memory non-programming economic research data with hypotheses, policy levers, and evidence cautions.

nodes.title: Household cost pressure
nodes.subtitle: Rent, utilities, food, transport, childcare
nodes.notes: Household pressure should be segmented by renters, homeowners, retirees, recent graduates, families with childcare, and car-dependent workers. Aggregate inflation hides different lived experiences across these groups.

nodes.title: Employer cost pressure
nodes.subtitle: Wages, inputs, credit, demand
nodes.notes: Small businesses face wage competition from anchor employers while absorbing higher input costs, rent, insurance, and credit costs. Hiring friction may persist even when job postings are open.

nodes.title: Policy levers
nodes.subtitle: Zoning, training, transit, grants
nodes.notes: Policy options include zoning reform, workforce training, transit access, childcare support, permitting improvements, and targeted small-business grants. Recommendations must separate immediate relief, capacity building, and structural reform.

nodes.title: Measurement limitations
nodes.subtitle: Lagging indicators and survey bias
nodes.notes: Data sources may lag conditions by months. Survey responses can overrepresent distressed firms. Labor-force participation shifts and neighborhood variation need explicit treatment before recommendations are made.

nodes.title: Working hypotheses
nodes.subtitle: Real wages and constraints
nodes.notes: Wage growth can coexist with lower real purchasing power when rent and insurance rise faster. Worker availability can be constrained by transit and childcare as much as by advertised wages.

nodes.title: Causation caution
nodes.subtitle: Do not overclaim evidence
nodes.notes: The brief must not turn correlation into causation without source evidence. Recommendations must cite which data supports them and where evidence is weak or contradictory.

projects.name: Urban Food Cooperative Operations Plan
projects.description: Operations plan for a member-owned urban food cooperative with retail, CSA pickup, and education programs.
projects.objective: Give Cognitive Memory a non-software operations project with governance, inventory, supplier, access, and financial-risk structure.

nodes.title: Member ownership model
nodes.subtitle: Shares, voting, access
nodes.notes: Members buy refundable ownership shares and receive voting rights. Non-members can shop. Members receive discounts and priority for limited CSA allocation, but essential food access cannot require volunteer labor.

nodes.title: Retail and CSA operations
nodes.subtitle: Staples, produce, prepared-food partners
nodes.notes: The storefront carries produce, dry goods, culturally relevant pantry items, and prepared-food partner products. CSA pickup requires allocation rules, spoilage handling, missed-pickup policy, and cold-chain checks.

nodes.title: Supplier policy
nodes.subtitle: Regional farms and transparent labor
nodes.notes: Supplier relationships prioritize regional farms, minority-owned producers, and transparent labor practices. The plan needs backup suppliers for weather, transportation disruption, and seasonal gaps.

nodes.title: Governance structure
nodes.subtitle: Board and advisory seats
nodes.notes: Board seats are elected by members with reserved advisory seats for neighborhood partners. Subsidy funds for food access must be reported separately from operating cash.

nodes.title: Inventory and access metrics
nodes.subtitle: Spoilage, shrink, donation, subsidy
nodes.notes: Measure spoilage, shrink, donation volume, subsidy usage, out-of-stock staples, member basket mix, prepared-food temperature exceptions, volunteer coverage, and supplier fulfillment weekly.

nodes.title: Operating risks
nodes.subtitle: Volunteer reliability and low margins
nodes.notes: Member enthusiasm may not translate to reliable volunteer coverage. Grocery margins are low even with strong community support. Subsidized pricing can become opaque without clear financial reporting.
